blocks.md: - Exponential functions of the form **y = a**<sup>**x**</sup> with **a > 0** are considered at A level

- All graphs of the form **y = a**<sup>**x**</sup> will pass through (0, 1) because **a**<sup>**0**</sup>** = 1**
- The **x**-axis is an **asymptote** ![Exponential Functions fig1, A Level & AS Maths: Pure revision notes](assets/f3129cff5153-6-1-1-exponential-functions-fig1.png)

- Where **x < 0** the higher value of **a** is the “lower” graph

  - e.g. $3^{x}<2^{x}$ when $x<0$
- Where **x > 0** the higher value of **a** is the “higher” graph

  - e.g. $3^{x}>2^{x}$ when $x>0$
- **a > 1** is **exponential** **growth **(see Exponential Growth & Decay)

blocks.alt: Exponential Functions fig3, A Level & AS Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md:
- Where **x < 0** the higher value of **a** is the “lower” graph

  - e.g. $0.3^{x}<0.2^{x}$ when $x<0$
- Where **x > 0** the higher value of **a** is the “higher” graph

  - e.g. $0.3^{x}>0.2^{x}$ when $x>0$
- **0 < a < 1** is **exponential decay**
- You may like to think about why** a = 1** is **not** considered... If a = 1, y = 1<sup>x</sup> = 1 for all values of x
